title: Inventory API 504s under burst load — cache stampede on invalidation
symptom: inventory-api returns 504 Gateway Timeout for a subset of requests during traffic peaks (flash sales, 2-4pm EST client peak). Redis hit rate drops sharply at the same moment.
rootCause: When a stock event invalidates a hot SKU key, hundreds of concurrent requests miss the cache at once and all query Postgres for the same row (cache stampede). DB latency climbs past the 5s gateway timeout.
resolution: 1) Enable request coalescing in inventory-api (INVENTORY_SINGLEFLIGHT=true) so only one request per key rebuilds the cache. 2) Replace delete-on-invalidate with write-through refresh for the top 500 SKUs. 3) If it recurs before a fix ships: temporarily raise the cache TTL to 120s via the feature flag inventory-cache-ttl.
prevention: Alert when Redis hit rate on inventory:* keys drops below 85%. Load test invalidation paths before large sales.

title: Checkout latency spike — Redis session cache evicting live sessions
symptom: checkout-service p95 latency jumps to 3-5s; users bounced back to cart; Redis evicted_keys metric climbing.
rootCause: The session Redis instance hit maxmemory with the volatile-lru policy while analytics keys had no TTL, so live session keys were evicted first.
resolution: 1) Set maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru on the session cluster. 2) Add a 24h TTL to analytics:* keys. 3) Raise maxmemory from 2GB to 4GB. Verify with redis-cli INFO stats that evicted_keys stops growing.
prevention: Grafana alert at 80% Redis memory. New key prefixes must declare a TTL in code review.

title: Safely rotating the auth signing certificate (JWKS cache pitfall)
symptom: After a scheduled signing-cert rotation, token refresh fails for a share of users with 'invalid signature'. Only pods that started before the rotation are affected.
rootCause: api-gateway caches the JWKS for 24h. The old key was removed at the same moment the new one was published, so gateways with a warm cache rejected tokens signed with the new key.
resolution: Rotation procedure: 1) Publish the NEW key to JWKS alongside the old key at least 24h before switching signing. 2) Switch auth-service to sign with the new key. 3) Remove the old key only after 24h (the max token + cache lifetime). Emergency fix used on the day: rolling restart of api-gateway to flush the JWKS cache. The JWKS cache TTL has since been reduced to 10 minutes (JWKS_CACHE_TTL=600).
prevention: Cert rotation is now a two-step change ticket with a 24h gap; checklist lives in the on-call runbook.

title: orders-db connection pool exhaustion — diagnosis and fix
symptom: Order API errors 'remaining connection slots are reserved' / 'too many clients'; failed order transactions; connection count on orders-db at 100/100.
rootCause: A batch job opened a new DB connection per query instead of using the shared pool.
resolution: 1) Check pg_stat_activity grouped by application_name to find the offender. 2) Pause the offending job (kubectl scale deploy/<job> --replicas=0). 3) Make sure traffic goes through pgBouncer (transaction mode, default_pool_size=20). 4) Fix the code to use db.getPool() — never new Client(). 5) Confirm connections drop below 80.
prevention: Alert at 80% connection utilisation; connection-pool usage is on the code review checklist; load test new batch jobs before prod.

title: How to release to production (and when you can't)
symptom: New joiners ask how a change reaches production and why their deploy was blocked.
rootCause: The release process was only ever explained verbally in KT sessions.
resolution: Merge to main → GitHub Actions builds and deploys to staging automatically → run smoke tests (npm run smoke -- --env=staging) → approve the 'promote-to-prod' job, which does a blue-green switch on EKS. Change freeze: no prod deploys on Fridays after 3pm IST or during client peak (2-4pm EST) without Raj's approval. Rollback: re-run the previous green deployment job.
